newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures underpined by short covering.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures underpined by short covering.

text.p: Short covering supported UK grain futures during a fairly quiet session on Wednesday.
Trading was within tight ranges with closing prices 0.20 to 0.30 stg up for wheat and 0.50 to 0.35 stg higher for barley.
"The market tried to go down in early dealings and failed and then tried to go up and failed again," said a trader.
"It was trading on the way down but not on the way up because many people are working out of very short books," said another.
Turnover were light with 354 lots on wheat and 38 lots on barley.
"The market is nearly always a dead duck on a Wednesday because people are worried about what may or may not happen at the weekly (EU) grain tender in Brussels on Thursday," said one trader.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures were unchanged after trading 10 lots all in October 1996.
UK fob trade was quiet with hardly a market reported while delivered trade was again mainly hand-to-mouth.
